# Introduction

This document includes the preprocessing workflow for Affymetrix exon microarrays (HuEx-1_0-st-v2) of postmortem human brain (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex - Brodmann area 9) samples coming from patients with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BPD) and major depression disorder (MDD) as well as healthy controls (CTL). The *.CEL* output files of the Affymetrix microarrays as well as the phenotype data file in *.csv* format are conduced as input for the workflow. Following steps will be performed: 

1. Load data, remove replicates and complement the phenotype data
2. Data calibration: background correction, normalization and summarization (to core gene and probeset level)
3. Remove controls, cross-hybridization (cross-hybridization only on probeset level) and chrX, chrY and chrM
4. Find hidden factors (SVA) and do batch correction using ComBat
5. Summarize to gene, transcript and exon level using a median approach
6. Annotation and removal of multiple mapped exons/transcripts to genes
7. Reduce genes, transcripts and exons with duplicated expression values (save info in annotation)

Below you can find the list of packages that are required by the workflow. 
```{r}
# General Bioconductor packages
library(BiocManager)
library(oligoClasses)

# Annotation and data import packages
library(pd.huex.1.0.st.v2) # for oligo::rma function
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicAlignments)

# Quality control and pre-processing packages 
library(oligo) # for background correction, normalization and summarization
library(sva) # for Combat and hidden batch correction

# Formatting packages
library(data.table)
library(dplyr) # for data transformation
library(tidyr)
```


# Generate output folders

Before we can start, we need to make sure that the output folder for the .RData files exists. If it does not exist yet, we will generate it using the systems (Red Hat Enterprise Linux operating system: Fedora 25) "mkdir" command. 
```{r}
outpath = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEA/01_RData_files"
system(paste0("mkdir -p ", outpath))
```


# Import Affymetrix data

Now, we will load the raw data *CEL* files produced by the Affymetrix array scanner software. These files contain the measured probe intensities. We also need to save the phenotype information for each sample. 

First, we generate a list including the *CEL* files and paths from a given directory.
```{r}
cel_files <- oligoClasses::list.celfiles("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/2018-07-11_gene_expression/raw_data", full.names = TRUE)
```

Now, we will save the phenotype information into a pData variable. The samples need to be in the same order as the CEL files are read in.
```{r}
pheno_data <- read.table("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/2019-04-09_sample_sheet_KW.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = T)
```

## Remove replicates

Our dataset includes five replicated samples, which we first need to remove from the *celFiles* and *pData* variable. 

| MHRI-ID |        Filename1 (2009)       |        Filename2 (2014)       |
|:-------:|:-----------------------------:|:-----------------------------:|
|  93.087 | afae2196-30-93.087-150709.CEL |   9.175_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL  |
|  93.046 | afae2196-35-93.046-150709.CEL | MU_9.174_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  97.214 |  afae2196-4-97.214-150709.CEL | MU_9_114_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  93.052 | afae2196-43-93.052-150709.CEL | MU_9_176_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  95.146 |  afae2196-6-95.146-150709.CEL | MU_9_107_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |

We will only remove the five older replicated files (from 2009). 
```{r}
replicates <- pheno_data[(duplicated(pheno_data$MHRIID) | duplicated(pheno_data$MHRIID, fromLast = TRUE)) & pheno_data$Batch == "A", "Filename"]
# remove the replicates from phenotype data
pheno_data <- pheno_data[-(which(pheno_data$Filename %in% replicates)), ] 
# remove replicates from cel file list
cel_files <- unlist(lapply(cel_files, function(x) if(!(strsplit(x, "/")[[1]][9] %in% replicates)) x)) 
```

## Complement phenotype data

Complement the phenotype data such that the diagnosis of schizophrena (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BPD) and major depression disorder (MDD) are changed to one case (CASE) only. Also add the quadratic RNA integrity number (RIN2).  
```{r}
# add original Dx as Diagnosis column to pData
pheno_data["Diagnosis"] <- pheno_data$Dx

# change BPD and MDD diagnosis (Dx) to SCZ
pheno_data$Dx <- as.character(pheno_data$Dx) # change factors to characters
pheno_data[pheno_data$Dx == "SCZ" | pheno_data$Dx == "BPD" | pheno_data$Dx == "MDD", "Dx"] <- "CASE" # change SCZ, BPD and MDD to CASE
pheno_data[, c("Sex", "Dx", "Suicide")] <- lapply(pheno_data[, c("Sex", "Dx", "Suicide")], factor)

# relevel disease (Dx) to control (CTL)
pheno_data$Dx <- factor(pheno_data$Dx, levels = c("CTL", "CASE"))

# add quadratic RIN 
pheno_data["RIN2"] <- pheno_data$RIN^2
```

## Read in CEL files

Finally, we can read in the CEL files and check if they are identical with the order of the filenames in pData.
```{r, results = 'hide'}
raw_data <- read.celfiles(cel_files) # affyExpressionFS/ExonFeatureSet
pheno_data <- pheno_data[order(pheno_data$Filename), ]
identical(as.character(pheno_data$Filename), colnames(exprs(raw_data)))
```

## Add pData to raw ExpressionSet

Then, we check if the sample names in the expression dataset are identical (and in the same order) with the filenames in pData. If they are identical, we can place the pData information into the ExpressionSet.
```{r}
if(identical(as.character(pheno_data$Filename), colnames(exprs(raw_data))) == TRUE){
  pData(raw_data) <- pheno_data
}
# change sample names to shorter versions
sampleNames(raw_data) <- as.character(pheno_data$ShortName)
dim(raw_data)
```

## Save raw data

After every long and time consuming step we will save the generated data into an RData file. This step is necessary, so that we do not need to run all above steps again. 
```{r}
save(raw_data, file = paste0(outpath, "/1_affymetrix_exon_microarray_raw_data.RData"))

# remove unneccessary data
rm(cel_files, pheno_data, replicates)
```


# Background Adjustment, Normalization and Summarization (RMA)

## To transcript/gene level

For the background correction, normalization and summarization oligos Robust Multichip Average (RMA) algorithm is standard practice and runs all three adjustments at once. 

To map the exon arrays to transcript/gene level, we have following three options: 

1. **core**: for all annotated RefSeq genes, 
2. **extended**: including RefSeq genes and genes with mRNA evidence, or 
3. **full**: including RefSeq genes, genes with mRNA evidence and genes with bioinformatic/computational prediction. 

As we want to use "safely" annotated genes we will set target to **core**. The RMA algorithm takes a while to process the huge amount of data provided by the Affymetrix microarrays. So, we will save the corrected data into an RData file for further analyses steps.
```{r}
core_summaries <- rma(raw_data, target = "core") 
dim(core_summaries)
save(core_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/2_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries.RData"))
```

We only summarized to transcripts to compare the resulting gene level to the probeset generated gene level. 

## To probeset level

For summarization to all three transcriptional levels (gene, transcript and exon level) it is possible to set target to **probeset** as done here:
```{r}
probeset_summaries <- rma(raw_data, target = "probeset") 
dim(probeset_summaries)
save(probeset_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/2_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries.RData"))
rm(raw_data)
```

For comparison reasons we will use the probeset summarized dataset for all three levels as we do not know what oligo (rma) is doing in the transcript level summarization and we filter for several steps on the probeset level.


# Filtering

Before, we can continue with our analysis, we need to filter controls, cross-hybridization probes and probes on chromosome X, Y and M. Therefore, we download the "HuEx-1_0-st-v2 Transcript Cluster Annotations, CSV, Release 36 (95 MB, 7/6/16)" and the "HuEx-1_0-st-v2 Probeset Annotations, CSV Format, Release 36 (58 MB, 7/6/16)" (filename after unzipping: HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.transcript.csv, HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.probeset.csv) under the "Current NetAffx Annotation Files" section on the Affymetrix support website (http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/byproduct.affx?product=huexon-st). These files contain all the neccessary information for the Affymetrix HuEx-1_0-st-v2 microarrays. All transcript cluster IDs and probeset IDs without a sequence start and stop information are removed from the datasets. 
```{r}
# Load Affymetrix Huex1.0stv2 transcript/gene annotation file (downloaded from the Affymetrix website)
huex_gene <- fread("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.transcript.csv", skip = 22, header = T, stringsAsFactors = F, data.table = F)
# remove ids with no start and stop information
huex_gene <- huex_gene[huex_gene$start != "---",]

# Load Affymetrix Huex1.0stv2 probeset annotation file (downloaded from the Affymetrix website)
huex_probeset <- fread("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.probeset.csv", skip = 22, header = T, stringsAsFactors = F, data.table = F)
# remove ids with no start and stop information
huex_probeset <- huex_probeset[huex_probeset$start != "---", ]
```

## Remove control data

The information about the type of probes is given in the column "category" or "probeset_type" of the HuEx information file. We will remove all transcript cluster IDs (core_summaries) and probeset IDs (probeset_summaries), which are not indicated with the "main" type.
```{r}
# show all gene categories and probeset types available
table(huex_gene$category)
table(huex_probeset$probeset_type)

# get all gene IDs with "main" category and all probeset IDs with "main" probeset type
transcript_ids <- huex_gene[huex_gene$category == "main", "transcript_cluster_id"]
probeset_ids <- huex_probeset[huex_probeset$probeset_type == "main", "probeset_id"]

# remove all transcript and probeset types, which are NOT "main" from the gene and probeset summary dataset
index <- which(rownames(exprs(core_summaries)) %in% as.character(transcript_ids))
core_summaries <- core_summaries[c(index), ]
dim(core_summaries)
index <- which(rownames(exprs(probeset_summaries)) %in% as.character(probeset_ids))
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[c(index), ]
dim(probeset_summaries)

# remove variables not neccessary anymore (especially as we reuse variable names)
rm(transcript_ids, probeset_ids, index)
```

## Remove cross-hybridization data

Microarray technology has one weakness: the fact that an RNA target sequence can bind to a short DNA probe that is not its exact complement, which is also called cross-hybridization. In the HuEx file, we also have the information in how many cross-hybridizations a probe is involved. All probes with a cross-hybridisation number of 1 and higher will be removed from the datasets. This is only necessary for the probeset data. For the gene dataset where are no cross-hybridization probes available anymore. 
```{r}
# show the number of cross-hybridizations per probe
table(huex_probeset$number_cross_hyb_probes)

# get all probeset IDs with zero/0 cross-hybridizations
probeset_ids <- huex_probeset[huex_probeset$number_cross_hyb_probes == 0, "probeset_id"]

# remove all probesets with cross-hybridization from the probeset summary dataset
index <- which(rownames(exprs(probeset_summaries)) %in% as.character(probeset_ids))
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[c(index), ]
dim(probeset_summaries)

# remove variables not neccessary anymore (especially as we reuse variable names)
rm(probeset_ids, index)
```

## Remove probesets on chrX, chrY and chrM

```{r}
# show all chromosomes available
table(huex_gene$seqname)
table(huex_probeset$seqname)

# get all transcript and probeset IDs with chrX, chrY and chrM
transcript_ids <- huex_gene[huex_gene$seqname %in% c("chrX", "chrY", "chrM"), "transcript_cluster_id"]
probeset_ids <- huex_probeset[huex_probeset$seqname %in% c("chrX", "chrY", "chrM"), "probeset_id"]

# remove all transcripts and probesets with chrX, chrY and chrM
index <- which(!(rownames(exprs(core_summaries)) %in% as.character(transcript_ids)))
core_summaries <- core_summaries[c(index), ]
dim(core_summaries)
index <- which(!(rownames(exprs(probeset_summaries)) %in% as.character(probeset_ids)))
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[c(index), ]
dim(probeset_summaries)

# remove variables not neccessary anymore (especially as we reuse variable names)
rm(transcript_ids, probeset_ids, index)
```

## Save data

Then, we save the datasets into RData files and remove unnecessary variables:
```{r}
save(core_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/3_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered.RData"))

save(probeset_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/3_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered.RData"))
```


# Batch correction

For the batch correction of the known batches of the microarrays, we will use ComBat from the Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) package. We have five batches (1: 64 samples, 2: 86 samples, 3,: 11 samples 4: 3 samples, A: 40 samples) included in the data. A plot as well as a more detailed description is given in the *02_QC_And_Plots.Rmd* script. The bach correction is done twice: 1) for the summarization based on core transcripts and 2) for the summarization on probeset level. 

## core_summaries

```{r}
exprs_raw <- as.matrix(exprs(core_summaries))
batch <- as.factor(pData(core_summaries)$Batch)
mod_combat <- model.matrix(~1, data = pData(core_summaries))
exprs_combat <- ComBat(dat = exprs_raw, batch = batch, mod = mod_combat, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)
# check if the two matrices are in the same order
identical(rownames(exprs(core_summaries)), rownames(exprs_combat)) 
exprs(core_summaries) <- exprs_combat
dim(core_summaries)
save(core_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/4_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected.RData"))
rm(exprs_raw, batch, mod_combat, exprs_combat)
```

## probeset_summaries

```{r}
exprs_raw <- as.matrix(oligo::exprs(probeset_summaries))
batch <- as.factor(pData(probeset_summaries)$Batch)
mod_combat <- model.matrix(~1, data = pData(probeset_summaries))
exprs_combat <- ComBat(dat = exprs_raw, batch = batch, mod = mod_combat, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)
identical(rownames(exprs(probeset_summaries)), rownames(exprs_combat)) # check if the two matrices are in the same order
exprs(probeset_summaries) <- exprs_combat
dim(probeset_summaries)
save(probeset_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/4_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected.RData"))
rm(exprs_raw, batch, mod_combat, exprs_combat)
```


# Hidden Batch Effects

For the hidden batch effects, we also will use SVA. Here, we first need to reduce the datasets to samples with complete phenotype data (from 204 samples to 169 samples). Then, we evaluate the number of SV required for the data. The package SVA provides a method, which helps to choose this number. As received surrogate variables will be integrated as a covariate into our design matrix for the differential expression analysis, we will include found surrogate variates into the pData of the summaries.

## Remove samples with missing values

As we have some missing values in the phenotype data, 26 mds (C1-C10) values, we first need to remove them from the microarrays as well as the phenotype dataset.
```{r, echo = F}
# remove all samples with C1 = NA 
index <- which(is.na(pData(core_summaries)$C1))
core_summaries <- core_summaries[, -c(index)]
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[, -c(index)]
rm(index)  # remove index (as we reuse the variable name beneath)

# remove all samples with Type_of_Death = NA 
index <- which(is.na(pData(core_summaries)$Type_of_Death))
core_summaries <- core_summaries[, -c(index)]
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[, -c(index)]
rm(index)  # remove index as we do not need this variable anymore

# check dim of Summaries (from 204 samples 25 rows should be removed = 169 samples left)
dim(core_summaries)
dim(probeset_summaries)
```

## core_summaries

Now, we can check the dataset for hidden factors considering all covariates we will use in the differential gene expression analysis.
```{r}
# setting up the data for SVA
pheno <- pData(core_summaries)
edata <- exprs(core_summaries)
mod <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4, data = pheno)
mod0 <- model.matrix(~ 1 + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4, data = pheno)

# Apply the sva function to estimate surrogate variables
nsv <- num.sv(edata, mod, method = "leek")  # estimate the number of latent factors
svobj <- sva(edata, mod, mod0, n.sv = nsv)  # => NO surrogate variables found
rm(pheno, edata, mod, mod0, svobj)  # remove unnecessary data

# save dataset
save(core_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA.RData"))
```

Here, num.sv estimated `r nsv` surrogate variables. As we did not find any surrogate variables, we do not need to include anything in the pData of the core_summaries.

## probeset_summaries

Now, we can check the dataset for hidden factors considering all covariates we will use in the differential gene expression analysis.
```{r}
# setting up the data for SVA
pheno <- pData(probeset_summaries)
edata <- exprs(probeset_summaries)
mod <- model.matrix(~ Dx + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4, data = pheno)
mod0 <- model.matrix(~ 1 + Age + Sex + pH + PMI + RIN + RIN2 + Suicide + Type_of_Death + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4, data = pheno)

# Apply the sva function to estimate surrogate variables
nsv <- num.sv(edata, mod, method = "leek")  # estimate the number of latent factors
svobj <- sva(edata, mod, mod0, n.sv = nsv) 
pData(probeset_summaries)$SV1 <- svobj$sv  # 1 surrogate variable found => add to pData

# save dataset
save(probeset_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA.RData"))
```

Here, num.sv estimated `r nsv` surrogate variable. As we found one surrogate variable, we will include it for further analyses in the pData of the probeset_summaries.

To check if the first surrogate variable is enough, we will also calculate the first 20 surrogate variables. We will save the results into an .RData file and generate a comparison plot in the QC (new .Rmd file) step.
```{r}
# save 1-20 surrogate variables (for sv selection plot)
svobj <- sva(edata, mod, mod0, n.sv = 20) 
save(svobj, file = paste0(outpath, "/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_surrogate_variables_1-20.RData"))
rm(svobj, nsv, edata, pheno, mod, mod0) # remove unnecessary data
```


# Mapping files

## GENCODE information

First, we need all gene, transcript and exon information for the human hg19 (GRCH37) genome. Therefore, we will load the Gencode release 19 .gtf file (downloaded from https://www.gencodegenes.org/human/release_19.html) and filter for all protein-coding genes as well as manually annotated genes from the HAVANA group (source). Then, we will split the dataset into gene, transcript and exon types only.
```{r}
# Load Gencode gtf file
gencode <- import.gff("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/annotation_files/gencode.v19.annotation.gtf", format = "gtf")
gencode <- gencode[gencode$gene_type == "protein_coding"]  # get only protein-coding genes
gencode <- gencode[gencode$source == "HAVANA"] # get only HAVANA source data
genes <- gencode[gencode$type == "gene"]  # get only genes (no exons, cds, transcripts etc.)
transcripts <- gencode[gencode$type == "transcript"]  # get only transcripts
exons <- gencode[gencode$type == "exon"]  # get only exons
rm(gencode)
```

Now, we need to generate the mapping files for the core based genes and the probeset based genes, transcripts and exons. 

## Affymetrix information

To summarize the core data to gene level, we need to map the transcript cluster IDs to Ensembl gene IDs. For the mapping to gene IDs we generate a GRanges Object out of the Affymetrix transcript information (chr, start, stop and transcript cluster ID) given in the HuEx file loaded in the **Filtering** section. 
```{r}
core_genes <- GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0(huex_gene$seqname)), 
                ranges = IRanges(start = as.numeric(as.character(huex_gene$start)), 
                end = as.numeric(as.character(huex_gene$stop))),
                id_internal_huex = huex_gene$transcript_cluster_id,
                gene_assignment = huex_gene$gene_assignment)
rm(huex_gene)
```

To summarize the probeset data to gene, transcript and exon level, we need to map the probeset IDs to gene IDs. For the mapping to gene IDs we generate a GRanges Object out of the Affymetrix probeset information (chr, start, stop and probeset ID) given in the HuEx file loaded in the **Filtering** section. 
```{r}
# Generate GRanges object for the probeset information (with chr, start, stop and probeset id)
probesets <- GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0(huex_probeset$seqname)), 
                     ranges = IRanges(start = as.numeric(as.character(huex_probeset$start)), 
                     end = as.numeric(as.character(huex_probeset$stop))),
                     id_internal_huex = huex_probeset$probeset_id,
                     gene_assignment = huex_probeset$gene_assignment)
rm(huex_probeset)
```


# Gene level (core)

## Generate the annotation file

For the core (transcript) based genes, we use all protein-coding genes (GENCODE) and overlap this dataset to our transcript IDs using their overlapping positions. All transcripts which overlap with more than one gene will later be removed from the core_summaries dataset. 
```{r}
# Merge the transcript ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(core_genes, genes, ignore.strand = T)
anno_genes_core <- mergeByOverlaps(core_genes, genes)
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, c("core_genes", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "gene_name", "gene_assignment")]
dim(anno_genes_core)
```

For all four (core genes, probeset genes, probeset transcripts and probeset exon) annotation files, we need to filter the datasets. As the filtering is exactly the same for all datasets, we will generate a function here, which we will use in all annotation filtering steps below. There are two filtering steps required: 
1. filter for genes, transcripts and exons which also include an Affymetrix HuEx gene assignment to the same gene name and
2. remove transcript/probeset IDs with multiple gene assignments/annotations. 
```{r}
FilterAnnotationFile <- function(anno){
  # 1. Get all rows, with the same Affymetrix Huex gene assignment as the gene name
  index <- unlist(sapply(1:length(anno$gene_name), function(x) if(grepl(anno$gene_name[x], anno$gene_assignment[x]) == TRUE) x))
  anno <- anno[c(index), ]
  print(dim(anno))

  # 2. Remove IDs with multiple gene assignments (or annotations)
  dt <- as.data.table(anno)
  id_counts <- dt[, .(number_of_distinct_orders = length(unique(gene_name))), by = id_internal_huex]
  ids_to_remove <- unique(id_counts[id_counts$number_of_distinct_orders > 1, ]$id_internal_huex)
  anno <- anno[!(anno$id_internal_huex %in% ids_to_remove), ]
  print(dim(anno))
  return(anno)
}
```

Now, we filter the core gene annotation file: 
```{r}
anno_genes_core <- FilterAnnotationFile(anno_genes_core)
```

## Summarization from transcripts to genes

To summarize the dataset based on gene IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble gene IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.
```{r}
# get transcript ID to Entrez gene ID mapping
mapping <- anno_genes_core[, c("id_internal_huex", "gene_id")]

# merge core expression matrix with the mapping file (to get gene IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(core_summaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex")
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to gene level using median expression (changed back to old version as it is exactly doing the same in less code!!!)
expr_dt <- data.table(expressions)
expr_dt <- expr_dt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'gene_id']
exprs_summarized <- as.matrix(expr_dt[, -1])
rownames(exprs_summarized) <- expr_dt$gene_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the gene summarized expressions. 
```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of exprs_summarized as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet
df <- matrix(NA, ncol = 1, nrow = length(rownames(exprs_summarized)))[, -1]
rownames(df) <- rownames(exprs_summarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
gene_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = exprs_summarized, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(core_summaries), 
                     featureData = data, 
                     experimentData = experimentData(core_summaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(core_summaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(gene_summaries)
```

Save the gene summarized data into an RData file and remove unnecessary data.
```{r}
# save data
save(gene_summaries, anno_genes_core, file = paste0(outpath, "/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_gene_summaries.RData"))

# remove unnecessary data
rm(core_genes, index, mapping, expressions, expr_dt, exprs_summarized, df, data,  core_summaries)
```

## Annotation

For the annotation we need the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data generated before. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset and save the annotated data into an RData file.
```{r}
anno_genes_core <- as.data.table(anno_genes_core)

# get min start and max stop position for one transcript
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, list(chr = core_genes.seqnames, 
                                          start = min(core_genes.start), 
                                          end = max(core_genes.end), 
                                          gene_id = gene_id, 
                                          gene_name = gene_name), 
                                  by = gene_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[!duplicated(anno_genes_core), ]
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6)]
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, c(7, 1:6)]
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7)]
anno_genes_core <- anno_genes_core[, c(2, 8, 7)]

# NO multiple ID to symbol mapping => no filtering of multiple mapped genes

# now join the expression dataset with the annotation 
fData(gene_summaries)$gene_id <- rownames(fData(gene_summaries))
fData(gene_summaries) <- dplyr::left_join(fData(gene_summaries), anno_genes_core)
rownames(fData(gene_summaries)) <- fData(gene_summaries)$gene_id
length(rownames(fData(gene_summaries)))
dim(gene_summaries)
```

Remove genes which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count genes multiple times (mostly genes with the same exons) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.
```{r}
# 1. Remove duplicated rows and merge rownames of duplicated rows together
expressions <- aggregate(rownames(exprs(gene_summaries)) ~., exprs(gene_summaries), paste, collapse = '|') 
rownames(expressions) <- expressions$`rownames(exprs(gene_summaries))` # change rownames to new merged rownames
expressions$`rownames(exprs(gene_summaries))` <- NULL  # remove rownames column

# 2. Merge the annotation of the merged rownames as well
anno_new <- data.frame()
for (rows in rownames(expressions)) {
  if (grepl("\\|", rows)) {
    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    ids_anno <- fData(gene_summaries)[rownames(fData(gene_summaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    ids_anno <- t(data.frame(apply(ids_anno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(ids_anno) <- rows
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, ids_anno)
  } else {
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, fData(gene_summaries)[rownames(fData(gene_summaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
gene_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = expressions, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(gene_summaries), 
                     featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(anno_new) , 
                     experimentData = experimentData(gene_summaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(gene_summaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(gene_summaries)
```

We do not have any NA's in the gene IDs and/or gene symbols, so we do not need to exclude them. Therefore, we can just save the annotated dataset into an RData file:
```{r}
save(gene_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/7_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_gene_summaries_annotated.RData"))
rm(anno_genes_core, anno_new, expressions, rows, ids, ids_anno, gene_summaries)
```

# Gene level (probesets)

## Generate the annotation file

For the annotation to gene level, we need the information of all genes. Therefore, we use the Gencode data loaded above and filter for gene IDs to build our annotation dataset. This generates the necessary probeset ID to gene ID mapping for the annotation. Then, we filter the dataset using the function generated above before we merge the annotation to our expression matrix.

```{r}
GenomicAlignments::findOverlaps(probesets, genes, ignore.strand = T)
anno_genes <- mergeByOverlaps(probesets, genes)
anno_genes <- anno_genes[, c("probesets", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "transcript_id", "exon_id", "gene_name", "gene_assignment")]
```

```{r}
                      exprs = exprs_summarized,
```

## Annotation

We need the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data generated before, but first we check if any probeset ID has no gene ID mapping (all probesets have a Gene ID given! => no filtering done here!).
```{r}
nrow(anno_genes)
anno_genes <- anno_genes[!is.na(anno_genes$gene_id), ]
nrow(anno_genes)
```

Some parts of the data can be mapped to several gene names. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset and save the annotated data into an RData file (code and text from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1384/v2).
```{r}
anno_genes <- as.data.table(anno_genes)

# get min start and max stop position for one gene
anno_genes <- anno_genes[, list(chr = probesets.seqnames, 
                              start = min(probesets.start), 
                              end = max(probesets.end), 
                              gene_id = gene_id, 
                              gene_name = gene_name), by = gene_id]
# remove duplicated gene_id column (column number 5)

# paste chr, start and stop together
anno_genes <- anno_genes[!duplicated(anno_genes), ]
anno_genes <- anno_genes[ , new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5)]
anno_genes <- anno_genes[ , c(6, 1:5)]
anno_genes <- anno_genes[ , location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6)]

rownames(fData(gene_summaries)) <- fData(gene_summaries)$gene_id
length(rownames(fData(gene_summaries)))
dim(gene_summaries)
```

Remove genes which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count genes multiple times (overlapping genes on the genome) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.
```{r}

    ids_anno <- t(data.frame(apply(ids_anno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(ids_anno) <- rows
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, ids_anno)
  } else {
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, fData(gene_summaries)[rownames(fData(gene_summaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
gene_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                      exprs = expressions, 
                      phenoData = phenoData(gene_summaries), 
                      featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(anno_new) ,
```

# Transcript Level

## Generate the annotation file

For the annotation to transcript level, we need the information of all transcripts and the transcript filtered Gencode data loaded above. This generates the necessary probeset ID to transcript ID mapping for the annotation. (hint: use transcript ID instead of transcript names, e.g. transcript name DCAF8-001 has two transcript IDs ENST00000368073.3 and ENST00000556710.1 and one of the transcript IDs should map to gene AL139011.2 with transcript name AL139011.2-001 instead of DCAF8 and DCAF8-001 => wrong mapping!!!). Then, we filter the dataset using the function above, before we merge it to our expression matrix.  
```{r}
# Merge the probeset ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(probesets, transcripts, ignore.strand = T)
anno_transcripts <- mergeByOverlaps(probesets, transcripts)
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, c("probesets", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "transcript_id", "exon_id", "gene_name", "gene_assignment")]
dim(anno_transcripts)
anno_transcripts <- FilterAnnotationFile(anno_transcripts)
```

## Summarization from probesets to transcripts

To summarize the dataset based on transcript IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble Transcript IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.
```{r}
# Load the probeset data (after filtering, batch correction and SVA)
load(paste0(outpath, "/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA.RData"))
dim(probeset_summaries)

# remove probesets that do not have a transcript id mapping
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[featureNames(probeset_summaries) %in% as.character(anno_transcripts$id_internal_huex), ]

# get probeset to Entrez Transcript ID mapping
mapping <- anno_transcripts[, c("id_internal_huex", "transcript_id")]
mapping <- mapping[!duplicated(mapping), ] # remove duplicated rows

# merge probeset expression matrix with the mapping file (to get transcript IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(probeset_summaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex", all.x = T)
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to transcript level using median expression
expr_dt <- data.table(expressions)
expr_dt <- expr_dt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'transcript_id']
exprs_summarized <- as.matrix(expr_dt[, -1])
rownames(exprs_summarized) <- expr_dt$transcript_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the transcript summarized expressions. 
```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of exprs_summarized as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet

row.names(df) <- row.names(exprs_summarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
transcript_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                           exprs = exprs_summarized, 
                           phenoData = phenoData(probeset_summaries), 
                           featureData = data, 
                           experimentData = experimentData(probeset_summaries), 
                           protocolData = protocolData(probeset_summaries), 
                           annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(transcript_summaries)
```

Save the transcript summarized data into an RData file and remove unnecessary data.
```{r}
# save data
save(transcript_summaries, anno_transcripts, file = paste0(outpath, "/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_transcript_summaries.RData"))

# remove unnecessary data
rm(transcripts, probeset_summaries, mapping, expressions, expr_dt, exprs_summarized, df, data)
```

## Annotation

We need the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data generated before, but first we check if any probeset ID has no gene ID mapping (all probesets have a Gene ID given! => no filtering done here!).
```{r}
nrow(anno_transcripts)
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[!is.na(anno_transcripts$gene_id), ]
nrow(anno_transcripts)
```

Some parts of the data can be mapped to several gene names. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset and save the annotated data into an RData file (code and text from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1384/v2).
```{r}
anno_transcripts <- as.data.table(anno_transcripts)

# get min start and max stop position for one transcript
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, list(chr = probesets.seqnames, start = min(probesets.start), end = max(probesets.end), gene_id = gene_id, gene_name = gene_name), by = transcript_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together

anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6)]
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, c(7, 1:6)]
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7)]
anno_transcripts <- anno_transcripts[, c(2, 8, 6, 7)]

fData(transcript_summaries) <- dplyr::left_join(fData(transcript_summaries), anno_transcripts)
```

Remove transcripts which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count transcripts multiple times (mostly transcripts of the same gene) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.
```{r}

    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    ids_anno <- fData(transcript_summaries)[rownames(fData(transcript_summaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    ids_anno <- t(data.frame(apply(ids_anno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(ids_anno) <- rows
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, ids_anno)
  } else {
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, fData(transcript_summaries)[rownames(fData(transcript_summaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet

                           exprs = expressions, 
                           phenoData = phenoData(transcript_summaries), 
                           featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(anno_new) ,
```

```{r}
rm(anno_transcripts, anno_summarized, anno_filtered, ids_to_exclude, expressions, anno_new, rows, ids, ids_anno, transcript_summaries)
```

# Exon Level

## Generate the annotation file

Then, we take the exon filtered GENCODE data and merge the Affymetrix huex_probeset information with it. This generates the necessary probeset ID to exon ID mapping as well as the mapping dataset for the annotation in the next section.
```{r}
# Merge the probeset ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(probesets, exons, ignore.strand = T)
anno_exons <- mergeByOverlaps(probesets, exons)
anno_exons <- anno_exons[, c("probesets", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "transcript_id", "gene_name", "exon_id", "exon_number", "gene_assignment")]
dim(anno_exons)
anno_exons <- FilterAnnotationFile(anno_exons)
```

## Summarization of probeset data to exon level

To summarize the dataset based on exon IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble Exon IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.
```{r}
# Load the probeset data (after filtering, batch correction and SVA)
load(paste0(outpath, "/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA.RData"))

# remove probesets that do not have an exon id mapping
probeset_summaries <- probeset_summaries[featureNames(probeset_summaries) %in% as.character(anno_exons$id_internal_huex), ]

# get probeset to Entrez Exon ID mapping
mapping <- anno_exons[, c("id_internal_huex", "exon_id")]
mapping <- mapping[!duplicated(mapping), ] # remove duplicated rows

# merge probeset expression matrix with the mapping file (to get exon IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(probeset_summaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex")
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to exon level using median expression
expr_dt <- data.table(expressions)
expr_dt <- expr_dt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'exon_id']
exprs_summarized <- as.matrix(expr_dt[, -1])
rownames(exprs_summarized) <- expr_dt$exon_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the exon summarized expressions. 
```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of expr.matrix as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet
df <- matrix(NA, ncol = 1, nrow = length(rownames(exprs_summarized)))[, -1]
row.names(df) <- row.names(exprs_summarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
exon_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", exprs = exprs_summarized, phenoData = phenoData(probeset_summaries), featureData = data, experimentData = experimentData(probeset_summaries), protocolData = protocolData(probeset_summaries), annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(exon_summaries)
```

We save the data again into an RData file.
```{r}
# save data
save(exon_summaries, anno_exons, file = paste0(outpath, "/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_exon_summaries.RData"))

# remove unnecessary data
rm(probesets, probeset_summaries, mapping, expressions, expr_dt, exprs_summarized, df, data)
```

## Annotation

For the annotation we use the anno dataset generated by the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data in the section before. We first check, if any probeset ID has no Gene ID mapping (all probesets have a Gene ID given! => no filtering done here!).
```{r}
nrow(anno_exons)
anno_exons <- anno_exons[!is.na(anno_exons$gene_id), ]
nrow(anno_exons)
```

Some parts of the data can be mapped to several gene names. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset. 
```{r}
anno_exons <- as.data.table(anno_exons)

# get min start and max stop position for one exon
anno_exons <- anno_exons[, list(chr = probesets.seqnames, start = min(probesets.start), end = max(probesets.end), transcript_id = transcript_id, gene_id = gene_id, gene_name = gene_name), by = exon_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together
anno_exons <- anno_exons[!duplicated(anno_exons), ]
anno_exons <- anno_exons[ , new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6, 7)]
anno_exons <- anno_exons[ , c(8, 1:7)]
anno_exons <- anno_exons[ , location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8)]
anno_exons <- anno_exons[ , c(2, 9, 6, 7, 8)]

# now remove exons with multiple gene id mappings
anno_summarized <- anno_exons[, .(count = uniqueN(gene_id)), by = exon_id]  # group by exon and count number of different Ensemble gene ids
anno_filtered <- as.list(anno_summarized[anno_summarized$count > 1, "exon_id"])  # get exon ids with multiple Ensemble gene ids
ids_to_exclude <- (featureNames(exon_summaries) %in% anno_filtered$exon_id)
exon_summaries <- subset(exon_summaries, !ids_to_exclude)  # remove multi-mapped exons
fData(exon_summaries)$exon_id <- rownames(fData(exon_summaries))
fData(exon_summaries) <- dplyr::left_join(fData(exon_summaries), anno_exons)
# because we included transcript IDs we need to merge them (several transcript IDs per exon possible!)
fData(exon_summaries) <- as.data.frame(unique(as.data.table(fData(exon_summaries))[, list(location, transcript_id = paste(transcript_id, collapse="|"), gene_id, gene_name), by = exon_id]))
rownames(fData(exon_summaries)) <- fData(exon_summaries)$exon_id
dim(exon_summaries)
```

Remove exons which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count transcripts multiple times (mostly exons of the same gene) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.
```{r}
# 1. Remove duplicated rows and merge rownames of duplicated rows together
expressions <- aggregate(rownames(exprs(exon_summaries)) ~., exprs(exon_summaries), paste, collapse = '|') 
rownames(expressions) <- expressions$`rownames(exprs(exon_summaries))`  # change rownames to new merged rownames
expressions$`rownames(exprs(exon_summaries))` <- NULL  # remove rownames column

# 2. Merge the annotation of the merged rownames as well
anno_new <- data.frame()
for (rows in rownames(expressions)) {
  if (grepl("\\|", rows)) {
    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    ids_anno <- fData(exon_summaries)[rownames(fData(exon_summaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    ids_anno <- t(data.frame(apply(ids_anno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(ids_anno) <- rows
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, ids_anno)
  } else {
    anno_new <- rbind(anno_new, fData(exon_summaries)[rownames(fData(exon_summaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
exon_summaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = expressions, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(exon_summaries), 
                     featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(anno_new), 
                     experimentData = experimentData(exon_summaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(exon_summaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
```
This reduced number of exons makes sense. Citation from the abstract of the publication from M. K. Sakharkar, V. T. Chow, and P. Kangueane (In Silico Biology, 2004): "The 26,564 annotated genes in the human genome (build October, 2003) contain 233,785 exons and 207,344 introns."

We do not have any NA's in the gene IDs and/or gene symbols, so we do not need to exclude them. Therefore, we can just save the annotated dataset into an RData file:
```{r}
dim(exon_summaries)
save(exon_summaries, file = paste0(outpath, "/7_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_batch_corrected_SVA_exon_summaries_annotated.RData"))
rm(anno_filtered, anno_summarized, anno_exons, ids_to_exclude, expressions, anno_new, ids, ids_anno)
```
